channel_justification: config_model['dm']['N2']==5 output channels map 1:1 onto config_data['r_types']==[protein, dna+rna, ion, ligand, lipid], so channel 0 is the protein-protein interface. Confirmed against interface_type_evaluation.ipynb, which forms pc=cat([1-max(p), p], dim=1) and reads class i at pc[:, i+1] with class_names=['protein','DNA/RNA','ion','ligand','lipid'] -- class 0 'protein' is therefore sigmoid(z[:,0]). z is logits; sigmoid is applied as in apply_model.ipynb. This model has no trained 'any interface' channel, so pesto_any records the notebook's own stand-in, max_c sigmoid(z[:,c]).
pesto_licence_note: Third-party comparator executed out-of-tree from its own clone. No PeSTo source is copied, vendored or redistributed by this script or its outputs; the outputs are per-residue numbers only.

alignment_proof.note: Had the scores been read off positionally, 18,179 of 176,842 keys (10.3%) across 60 of 561 contexts would have been given a different residue's score, silently. PeSTo parses the whole antigen including assembly copies of chains that are not declared antigen chains, and hetero groups, so its residue list is neither the same length nor the same order as our key list in 262 contexts.

falsification_tests.duplicate_owner_corruption_is_rejected: Mapping two distinct residue identities to one key index raises AssertionError('two residue rows claim the same key') -- the injectivity guard fires rather than silently keeping one.
falsification_tests.unscorable_key_yields_null_in_place: A fabricated residue identity inserted at position 100 of the key list comes back as null at exactly position 100, with all 100 keys before it and all 207 keys after it bit-identical to the baseline run. The array is not shifted, which is the specific failure mode that would invalidate the comparison.
falsification_tests.per_row_unanimity: Every residue row's atoms must agree on their provenance id or the run aborts; this held for all 561 contexts.

training_overlap.verdict: Overlap CANNOT be ruled out, and it is demonstrably present on the side we score. PeSTo's scores on this benchmark must be reported as optimistic.
training_overlap.training_data: First bioassembly of all PDB biological assemblies (paper Methods/'Datasets': 'The dataset is composed of all the biological assemblies from the Protein Data Bank'; Methods/'Training': 'We trained only on the first bioassembly provided by the PDB database'; consistent with config.py 'max_ba': 1). Fetched by live rsync with no date pin (upstream-pesto/data/rsyncPDB.sh).
training_overlap.stated_date_cutoff_note: No cutoff is stated anywhere: checked README.md, pesto.yml, data/rsyncPDB.sh, data/datasets/README.md, processing/split_dataset.ipynb, processing/build_dataset.py, the i_v4_1 config and slurm logs, and the paper's Methods and Data availability sections.
training_overlap.derived_date_bound_note: DERIVED BY US, not an authors' claim: RCSB initial_release_date resolved for all 30,629 resolvable entries in the shipped split lists whose id begins 6-9 gives a maximum release date of 2021-03-03, with releases falling to zero after it (2021-01: 418, 2021-02: 405, 2021-03: 96, then none). The checkpoint is dated 2021-09-07, which bounds it from above independently.
training_overlap.redundancy_filtering: 30% sequence identity, cluster level (paper Methods/'Datasets': 'The subunits are clustered using a maximum of 30% sequence identity between clusters'), using RCSB bc-30.out (named only in processing/split_dataset.ipynb, not the paper).
training_overlap.antibody_handling: Neither excluded nor specially handled; not stated in the paper or the code. A grep for antibod|immunoglob|epitope|paratope|nanobod across all source in the clone returns zero matches. Immunoglobulin chains land mostly in the held-out split as an incidental side effect of 30% clustering (8.9% of a 448-subunit validation sample vs ~0.2% genuine in a 472-subunit train sample), but that is a side effect, not a design choice, and it is incomplete -- genuine antibody chains remain in train (e.g. 6S3T_D, 6MHR_C, 6OYH_C, 5CJX_G).
training_overlap.why_antigens_are_not_protected: We score the ANTIGEN, and antigens are not protected by the antibody-side clustering effect. Training labels for a subunit are OR'd over every contacting partner in its bioassembly regardless of which split that partner went to (src/dataset.py select_by_sid masks only the target subunit; model/data_handler.py Dataset.__getitem__ ORs over all ckeys). The guard that would have prevented this, select_complete_assemblies, exists in src/dataset.py but is never called -- model/save/i_v4_1_2021-09-07_11-21/main.py imports only select_by_sid, select_by_max_ba and select_by_interface_types. So where an antigen chain is in train and its first bioassembly contains the Fab, that antigen's epitope was a positive protein-protein training label.

measured_overlap_this_benchmark.method: Exact per-subunit id join of each context's PDB id + declared antigen auth chain ids against subunits_train_set.txt (376,216 entries, read via 'git cat-file -p HEAD:data/datasets/subunits_train_set.txt' because the working-tree copy is a sparse 0-block file that reads as empty).
measured_overlap_this_benchmark.caveats: A train-list hit is an UPPER bound on exact-chain exposure: PeSTo's HDF5 filters (max_ba=1, <=8192 atoms, >=48 residues, must have a contact of a selected type) cut 376,216 subunits to 113,805 actually trained on. A MISS is not safety: 30% clustering means a homolog of an antigen may be in train even when that exact chain is not, and bounding that needs a sequence search, not an id join.

homolog_level_bound.method: Antigen chains joined to RCSB 30%-identity clusters (bc-30.out, shipped in upstream-pesto/data/datasets/), then asked whether any cluster-mate appears in subunits_train_set.txt. This is the homolog-level analogue of the exact join, at the identity threshold PeSTo itself clustered on.
homolog_level_bound.coverage_caveat: 168 of 561 antigen chains are absent from the shipped bc-30.out, so no bound is computable for them. That file is a LATER RCSB download than the one used to build the splits (533,352 sids, vs 575,340 across the three split files, with 19,305 train sids missing from it), so it is an imperfect instrument.
homolog_level_bound.interpretation: Homolog-level exposure to the TRAIN split is 31.8% of covered contexts (33.3% of covered test contexts), roughly double the 17.5% exact-chain figure. But 99.7% of covered contexts have a 30%-identity cluster-mate somewhere in PeSTo's PDB snapshot, which is unavoidable for a model trained on all of PDB and means 'did it see a homolog' is not a discriminating question. The discriminating question is epitope-LABEL exposure, which is what the exact-chain join (17.5%) and the train-cluster join (31.8%) measure.

measured_effect_on_scores.note: Stratification of the test-split signal by leak status. Not the real evaluation, but it shows the leak is not hypothetical. The pooled-residue figures came first; the macro figures below use the project's own aggregation (within-instance AUROC, mean within cluster, mean across clusters) on the 110 evaluated test interfaces, so they are the ones comparable to the published comparator numbers.
measured_effect_on_scores.headline: On the project's own macro aggregation, PeSTo scores 0.6521 over all 110 test interfaces but only 0.6235 on the 95 whose antigen chain is NOT in its training list, versus 0.7487 on the 15 that are. The clean figure is the honest comparator baseline; the all-interfaces figure is inflated by the leaked minority.
measured_effect_on_scores.interpretation: On the 14 test contexts whose antigen chain is in PeSTo's training list, AUROC is 0.870 and the epitope mean is 5x the non-epitope mean. On the 91 clean contexts, AUROC is 0.629 and the epitope/non-epitope separation is +0.010, i.e. almost nothing. The pooled number is inflated by the leaked 13%; the clean-only figure is the honest comparator baseline.
